title: desktop: LinkedIn import via DOM capture keeps site-branded title and falls back to hostname as company
body: ## Summary When the extension imports a LinkedIn job posting using its DOM-capture ("Scan mode") path, the desktop backend's generic HTML fallback produces a title still carrying the page's site-branding suffix and a company name that is just the URL hostname, even though the real employer name is present elsewhere in the captured markup. ## Environment Extension 0.154.0 (store build), desktop app 0.154.0, Windows 11, Chrome. ## Steps to reproduce 1. As a logged-in LinkedIn user, open a job view page (`https://www.linkedin.com/jobs/view/`). 2. Trigger the extension popup or side panel and click Import. ## Expected - Title: the job title alone (e.g. "Javascript Developer"). - Company: the real employer name (e.g. "Digital Waffle"). ## Actual - Title is saved as the whole `` tag verbatim, including site branding, e.g. `"Javascript Developer | Digital Waffle | LinkedIn"`. - Company is saved as the URL host, e.g. `"www.linkedin.com"`. - DOM capture itself succeeded (the stored job description was ~8,000 characters of real content, including the text "Company logo for, Digital Waffle" from an `<img alt>`) — the extraction heuristic just never looks at that signal. - Frequency: reproduced on the one LinkedIn posting tested; deterministic given the code path (not timing-dependent). ## Evidence Imported application record: `title` = `"Javascript Developer | Digital Waffle | LinkedIn"`, `company` = `"www.linkedin.com"`, with the correct job URL and a full-length job description containing the real company name as incidental text (not extracted as a field). ## Root cause Scan-mode Import (`apps/desktop/src-tauri/src/extension_bridge/import_flow.rs:252`) parses the extension's captured DOM directly via `scraping::scrape_url::parse_from_html`, bypassing the dedicated LinkedIn board handler (which needs the desktop's own authenticated session and isn't needed when the DOM was already captured from the owner's logged-in browser). That generic path has two gaps: - `parse_generic_html` (`apps/desktop/src-tauri/src/scraping/scrape_url/mod.rs:918-931`, called at `mod.rs:468`) takes the first `<title>`/`<h1>` element's full text with no trimming of a trailing " | SiteName" suffix. - `parse_generic_company` (`apps/desktop/src-tauri/src/scraping/scrape_url/mod.rs:939-969`) only checks JSON-LD `hiringOrganization.name` and `meta[property="og:site_name"]`; neither is populated by LinkedIn's authenticated, client-rendered job page. Its caller (`mod.rs:549`) then falls back to the bare URL host (`parse_generic_company(html).unwrap_or(host)`). ## Suggested fix direction In the generic fallback: strip a trailing `" | <site>"`/`" - <site>"` suffix from the title when it matches a known site name or `og:site_name`; and add a company fallback that looks for a distinctive `<img alt="Company logo for, X">`-style pattern (or similar DOM signal already present in LinkedIn's captured markup) before giving up and using the host.

title: extension: Import silently captures the embedding page for iframe-embedded ATS boards
body:
## Summary

When a job board is embedded on a company's own careers page via a cross-origin `<iframe>` (a common pattern for Ashby, and potentially other ATS platforms with embeddable widgets), clicking **Import** on the wrapper page silently imports the WRAPPER page's own title/heading instead of the job posting inside the iframe. There is no error, no partial-capture warning — only a very low match-fit percentage in the success toast, which is easy to miss or not recognize as a signal that anything went wrong.

## Environment

- Extension 0.154.0 (store build)
- Desktop app 0.154.0
- Windows 11, Chrome

## Steps to reproduce

1. Open a careers page that embeds an ATS job board (e.g. Ashby) in a cross-origin `<iframe>`, with the specific job selected via a query parameter in the outer page's URL.
2. Click the extension's toolbar icon to open the popup on that tab.
3. Click **Import this job**.

## Expected

Either the real job posting inside the iframe is captured and imported, or the user is clearly told the capture may not reflect the actual posting (e.g. the existing "couldn't read the description — open AI Job Hunter to paste it" partial-import warning), so they know to check/complete the record manually.

## Actual

The import succeeds with a confident-looking message ("Imported \"<wrapper page's own heading>\". Open AI Job Hunter → Applications to view it.") built from the OUTER page's own `<title>`/`<h1>`, not the job. The only anomaly visible to the user is a very low percent-fit suffix on that same message — there is no explicit warning, and the resulting Application record has the wrong title/company and no real job description. Frequency: deterministic, every time, for any cross-origin-iframe-embedded ATS whose wrapper page happens to render a non-empty title/heading (not timing-dependent).

## Evidence

Reproduced against a live Ashby-embedded careers page; the popup's success message named the wrapper page's own "Careers at <company>"-style heading rather than the actual job title, at a single-digit percent fit. (Sanitized — no personal data; the specific company/job-posting URL used for the repro is omitted here as it is not needed to understand or fix the defect.)

## Root cause

- `apps/extension/src/background.ts:474-477` (`captureTabHtml`) injects the DOM-capture script via `browser.scripting.executeScript({ target: { tabId }, files: ['content.js'] })` with no `allFrames` option, so `content.ts`'s capture (`document.documentElement.outerHTML`) can only ever see the top-level document — a cross-origin iframe's content is unreachable without `host_permissions` this extension does not request. (The README already documents this exact no-allFrames/activeTab-only trade-off for the Fill feature — `apps/extension/README.md`'s "Known limit — assisted autofill fills the TOP-LEVEL document only" note — but not for Import.)
- `apps/desktop/src-tauri/src/scraping/scrape_url/mod.rs:466-548` (`parse_from_html`) falls through to the whole-document `<title>`/first-`<h1>` fallback when the extension's job-root hint finds nothing in the outer page (which it never can here), picking up the wrapper page's own heading.
- `apps/desktop/src-tauri/src/scraping/scrape_url/mod.rs:129-191` (`canonical_job_url`) and `apps/desktop/src-tauri/src/scraping/ats_ref.rs:131-138` (`ashby_slug`) only recognize a URL whose OWN host is the ATS's host — nothing detects/resolves an embedded ATS iframe on an unrelated host.
- `apps/desktop/src-tauri/src/extension_bridge/import_flow.rs:103-105` (`usable()`) treats ANY non-empty title as usable, so the wrapper page's own heading (never empty) suppresses the existing "couldn't read the description" partial-import warning (`apps/extension/src/job-tools/job-tools.ts:80-127`) that would otherwise flag this case.

## Suggested fix direction

Either direction addresses the silent-wrong-data problem without requiring new cross-origin permissions:

1. **Cheap, in line with the existing Fill precedent**: extend the README's documented Fill limitation to Import, and have the extension/desktop side detect "no job-root hint was found in the outer document AND the page contains a same-page ATS iframe" (a `document.querySelector('iframe[src*="ashbyhq.com"], iframe[src*="greenhouse.io"], ...')` check in `content.ts` is enough signal) to surface the iframe's own URL to the user (e.g. "This job is embedded — open it directly at <iframe src> to import").
2. **Fuller fix**: teach `usable()`/`import_flow.rs` that a title sourced only from the whole-document fallback (never from JSON-LD, `__NEXT_DATA__`, or the extension's own job-root hint) is a weaker signal, and route that case through the existing `partial` warning path instead of treating it as a clean success.

title: desktop: Open/Generate/Prepare in the app deep links never navigate on Windows (ajh://open/?url= rejected)
body:
## Summary

The extension's **"Open in app"**, **"Generate in the app"** and **"Prepare in the app"** links bring the desktop window to the front but never navigate. The app stays on whatever page it was showing. `ajh://settings/extension` ("Find my token") works on the same machine.

## Environment

Extension 0.154.0 (store build), desktop app 0.154.0 on Windows 11, Chrome. The machine has both the Microsoft Store package and the regular installer build installed. Windows resolves `ajh://` to the Store package, which hands the launch off to the already-running instance.

## Steps to reproduce

1. With the desktop app running, click **Open in app** in the extension's side panel on a tracked posting. Or run `start "" "ajh://open?url=<percent-encoded posting url>"` from a shell.
2. Watch the desktop window.

## Expected

The app navigates to that job's application page. With no match, it falls back to the Jobs list filtered by the URL, per `resolveJobDeepLinkTarget`.

## Actual

The window is shown and focused, and nothing else happens: no navigation, not even the Jobs fallback. This is deterministic, reproduced every time. `ajh://settings/extension` triggered the same way navigates correctly.

## Evidence

The command line the relaunched instance actually receives, read directly from the process:

```
<Store package>\ajh-tauri.exe ajh://open/?url=https%3A%2F%2Fjobs.smartrecruiters.com%2F...
```

Note the `/` inserted after `open`. The extension builds `ajh://open?url=…` (`apps/extension/src/sidepanel/sidepanel.ts`, `documents/documents.ts`, `prep/prep.ts`). Windows protocol activation canonicalises a URL whose path is empty by adding a trailing slash after the authority. `ajh://settings/extension` has a non-empty path, so it arrives unchanged, which is why it works.

## Root cause

1. **The slash-inserted form is rejected.** `apps/desktop/src-tauri/src/deeplink/mod.rs` `parse_job_url_target` does `rest.split_once('?')` and requires the action to be exactly `open` / `generate` / `prep`, so `open/` is rejected. `parse_one` then rejects it too (`rest.contains('?')`), so `parse_focus_target` returns `None`. The single-instance callback in `apps/desktop/src-tauri/src/lib.rs` has already called `tray::show_focus`, and `handle_deep_link(None)` does nothing. `deeplink/test.rs` only exercises the exact `ajh://open?url=` form.
2. **Cold start drops the intent (separate defect, same links).** When the app is *not* running, the cold-start block in `lib.rs` `setup()` calls `handle_deep_link` → `tray::dispatch_menu` before `tray::build` has managed `tray::PendingMenu` (`tray/mod.rs`). `try_state::<PendingMenu>()` returns `None`, the buffered intent is silently dropped, and the early emits fire before the renderer listens. The sibling `PendingFocus` (autopilot link) was already moved above that block for exactly this reason; `PendingMenu` was not. This affects all four `menu:navigate` deep links, including `settings/extension`, on a cold launch.
3. **No diagnostics.** The only log line on this path, `log::info!("[menu] dispatch …")` in `tray::dispatch_menu`, is under the `ajh_tauri::tray` target. That target sits below the global `Warn` level set in `lib.rs`'s log plugin builder, so a rejected link and a successful dispatch both leave nothing in the log.

## Suggested fix direction

- In `parse_job_url_target`, accept an optional single trailing `/` on the action (`open/?url=`, `generate/?url=`, `prep/?url=`). Keep every other rule (one `url=` param, length cap, http(s) with an authority). Add tests for the slash form and for a still-rejected `open//?url=` / `open/x?url=`.
- Manage `tray::PendingMenu` in `setup()` next to `PendingFocus`, before the cold-start deep-link block.
- Log a rejected `ajh://` argv at `warn` (scheme and action only, never the full URL) and raise the dispatch line to a logged level.
- Side note: `tauri_plugin_sentry` is registered before `tauri_plugin_single_instance`. That contradicts the in-code comment "Single-instance must be the FIRST plugin". It isn't the cause here, but worth aligning.

title: Appearance settings (theme, default panel tab) don't live-sync to an already-open panel
body:
## Summary

Two Appearance settings (Theme, Default panel tab) don't reliably reach a side panel that is already open in the same window — confirmed live, twice, with before/after screenshots. Neither is data loss and neither claims false success, but both are silent: nothing tells the user the change didn't apply to what's currently on screen.

## Environment

extension 0.154.0 store build, desktop app 0.154.0, Windows 11, Chrome. Found during an end-to-end test of the Settings page.

## 1. Theme doesn't live-sync to an already-open panel

### Steps to reproduce

1. Open the side panel in a window (any tab).
2. In a separate Settings tab, change Theme from Dark to Light.

### Expected / Actual

Settings itself updates immediately (confirmed via screenshot: `Theme: Light` selected, cream background). The already-open panel stays on the old theme (screenshot: still the dark background) — no repaint. Closing and reopening the panel picks up the new theme correctly, so the setting itself is fine; only the live surface is stale.

### Root cause

`apps/extension/src/lib/theme.ts` — `bootTheme()` runs once per surface load; there's no `chrome.storage.onChanged` listener repainting an already-mounted surface.

## 2. Default panel tab is masked by per-window session memory

### Steps to reproduce (directly reproduced)

1. Window A: open the panel (Default panel tab = Job at the time) — it opens on Job, as expected. Manually click over to the Answers tab.
2. Close the panel and reopen it in the **same** window A (Default panel tab setting unchanged).
3. Separately, Window B (freshly opened, panel never used in it before): open the panel — it opens on Job, matching the default. Change Default panel tab to Answers in Settings. Reopen the panel in the **same** window B.

### Expected / Actual

Step 2: reopening in window A shows **Answers** — the tab the user last clicked to, correctly remembered per-window across a close/reopen.

Step 3: reopening in window B shows **Answers** too, but here that's because it now matches the live default — window B never had an explicit tab switch, so it falls through to `getDefaultPanelTab()` and correctly reflects the change.

Not directly re-tested, but a direct reading of the code below: once a window's session memory holds a tab (from an explicit switch, as in window A), the fallback to `getDefaultPanelTab()` is skipped unconditionally — nothing re-checks whether a *later* Default-panel-tab change should override it. So a window like A, after a manual switch, would keep showing its remembered tab on reopen even if the default is changed afterward, until that window is closed. This half of the claim should be verified directly (switch tabs in a window, then change the default, then reopen in that same window) before being treated as confirmed rather than inferred.

### Root cause

`apps/extension/src/sidepanel/sidepanel.ts` — `loadActiveTab` only falls back to `getDefaultPanelTab()` when `storage.session` has no persisted tab for that window; a window where the user switched tabs at least once keeps its own memory until the window closes.

## Suggested fix direction

Add a `chrome.storage.onChanged` listener in the panel (and any other already-mounted surface) for the `theme` and `defaultPanelTab` keys, at minimum repainting the theme live; for the default-tab case, either clear the per-window session entry when the setting changes, or accept the current behavior as intentional ("remembers where you were") and say so in the Settings copy so it doesn't read as unconditional.

_Found during an end-to-end test of the published 0.154.0 extension against the 0.154.0 desktop app._

title: Prep tab gets stuck on unlabeled "Loading…" (draft buttons still enabled) when the active tab isn't a readable page
body:
## Summary

The side panel's **Prep** tab has three visually-identical-but-different states that all render as bare `Loading…`: (1) genuinely loading, (2) the page hasn't granted the extension `activeTab` access yet, and (3) the window's active tab is a non-content page (e.g. a pending `ajh://` deep-link tab). In cases 2 and 3 it never resolves on its own, the `Draft company brief` / `Draft salary answer` buttons stay visibly enabled the whole time, and there's no indication anything is wrong — unlike the **Job** tab, which correctly shows "Click the toolbar icon to grant access to this page" for case 2.

## Environment

extension 0.154.0 store build, desktop app 0.154.0, Windows 11, Chrome.

## Repro A — fresh navigation before activeTab is (re-)granted

1. Open the side panel, go to **Prep**.
2. `navigate_page`/type a new URL into the same tab (no toolbar click).
3. Prep tab: `Loading…` + both draft buttons enabled, indefinitely.
4. Switch to the **Job** tab on the same panel: correctly shows "Click the toolbar icon to grant access to this page, then use these tools."
5. Click the toolbar icon to grant access, switch back to Prep: now correctly shows `Nothing yet for this job.` + `Prepare in the app`.

## Repro B — "Prepare in the app" opens a pending tab that becomes active

1. On a job with no Prep content, click **Prepare in the app** (`browser.tabs.create({url:'ajh://prep?url=...'})`).
2. This opens a **new tab in the same window** for the `ajh://` external-protocol handoff, which becomes the window's active tab while Chrome's own external-app confirmation is pending.
3. Prep tab: reverts from `Nothing yet for this job.` back to bare `Loading…` (draft buttons still enabled) for as long as that pending tab is active.
4. Closing that pending tab (`chrome.tabs.remove`) and refocusing the original job tab self-heals Prep back to the correct empty state.

## Expected

Either a state-specific message (mirroring the Job tab's "click the toolbar icon…" message) or, at minimum, `Loading…` shouldn't be indistinguishable from "actually loading" when it's actually "no valid page to read right now" — and it shouldn't require the user to know to switch tabs/panel-tabs to recover.

## Actual

Bare, permanent `Loading…` with fully-clickable Draft buttons in both cases; self-heals only once the active tab becomes a valid job page again, with no hint to the user about what to do.

## Suspected cause

`prep/prep.ts`'s render logic (`renders statusText||'Loading…'`, per the existing code-map notes for this area) falls back to the generic `'Loading…'` whenever `statusText` is unset — which happens whenever `isPageTrusted(state)` never resolves to a definite trusted/untrusted value (state stays `null`) rather than explicitly reaching the "no page" case the Job tab already handles separately. `sidepanel/sidepanel.ts`'s population gate (`prep.refresh()`/`prep.reset()` around lines 405-414) is the likely place a "no valid active tab" branch is missing relative to what the Job tab's own component already does.

## Note re: automation vs. real behavior

In Repro B, the deep link itself never reached the desktop app during the automated test (no matching log line) — that part is very likely an automation artifact (Chrome's native external-protocol confirmation dialog needs a real user click, which an automated test can't perform) and is **not** part of this finding. The Prep-tab-freezes-while-that-pending-tab-is-active behavior is independent of whether the user ultimately accepts or declines that dialog, and would affect a real user identically either way.

_Found during an end-to-end test of the published 0.154.0 extension against the 0.154.0 desktop app._

title: Side panel left open across an auto-tracked submit shows stale (pre-apply) status
body:
## Summary

When the side panel is already open on a job's page *before* auto-track's submit-detection marks that job "applied" (a real form submit, or the fake-form technique used for E2E testing), the panel's **Job** tab keeps showing the old, pre-apply state (`Import this job` primary button, no stage tracker, `Answers` tab with no count) even well after the write has landed. A brand-new popup or a freshly-reopened panel shows the correct "Applied" state immediately — only the *already-open* surface is stale.

## Environment

extension 0.154.0 store build, desktop app 0.154.0, Windows 11, Chrome.

## Steps to reproduce

1. Import a fresh, untracked posting; keep the side panel open on that tab throughout.
2. Arm the watcher (`Check fit`) and submit the page's application form (a 3-field fake form was used for testing, but this is about the panel's own state, not the watcher itself).
3. Confirm the desktop side actually applied it: `ajh-tauri agent job "<url>"` → `"applied": true`.
4. Look at the still-open side panel's **Job** tab (no interaction other than switching its own internal tabs) — waited 17s+, tried switching Job/Answers/Job tabs internally.
5. Compare against a **freshly opened** popup/panel on the same tab.

## Expected

The already-open panel converges on the true state shortly after the write (it doesn't need to be instant, but it shouldn't stay wrong indefinitely with no user action available to fix it short of closing and reopening the panel).

## Actual

- Stale panel (open since before the submit): `Import this job` button, no stage tracker, `Answers` tab (no count) — indistinguishable from "never imported."
- Same tab, freshly triggered popup: `Applied Sep 21` status pill, correct.
- Same tab, side panel closed and reopened: `Applied Sep 21` + full `Saved → Applied → Interview → Offer` stage tracker, correct.

So the data is correct from the moment of the write; only the continuously-mounted panel component fails to pick it up. A user who leaves the panel open while filling out and submitting an application (the exact intended save-answers-on-submit + auto-track workflow) never sees confirmation that anything happened unless they close and reopen the panel.

## Suspected cause

The panel's Job-tab status likely isn't re-fetched on `submitDetected`/`status.update` success — only on its own mount (`start()`) or an explicit `getStatus`-triggering user gesture (per `connection-status.ts`). Auto-track's background flow (`background.ts`'s `handleSubmitDetected` → `lib/auto-track.ts`) doesn't appear to broadcast a refresh to already-open surfaces after a successful `updateStatus`. Worth checking whether the Job tab's data source subscribes to the same broadcast channel the Notification Center / badge nudge use, or only ever polls on mount.

_Found during an end-to-end test of the published 0.154.0 extension against the 0.154.0 desktop app._

title: Prep tab's Cancel does not actually stop the in-flight AI request (still billed in full)
body:
## Summary

Clicking **Cancel** on a Prep-tab on-demand draft (`Draft company brief` / `Draft salary answer`) correctly reverts the extension UI back to the draft button, but the underlying AI-provider request is **not aborted** — it runs to completion server-side and consumes real tokens/cost, exactly as if Cancel had never been clicked.

## Environment

extension 0.154.0 store build, desktop app 0.154.0, Windows 11, Chrome, provider `ollama-cloud` / `gpt-oss:20b`.

## Steps to reproduce

1. Open the side panel's **Prep** tab on any job with no existing company-brief/salary-answer content.
2. Click **Draft salary answer**.
3. Immediately click **Cancel** (verified via script: the Cancel button is clicked at the first opportunity, effectively 0ms after the draft starts, well before the ~3.5s the request actually takes).
4. Compare the extension's own click timestamp against the desktop app log (`AI Job Hunter.log`, UTC).

## Expected

Cancelling stops the outbound AI request; no further tokens are spent for that draft once Cancel is clicked.

## Actual

The app log shows the request completing in full, at the same duration/token cost as an un-cancelled draft:

```
[21:32:34] [ai] → req=29 provider=ollama-cloud model=gpt-oss:20b endpoint=/chat/completions streaming=true
[21:32:37] [ai] stream start job=job-6a6f0064-...
[21:32:37] [ai] stream end provider=ollama-cloud model=gpt-oss:20b answerLen=112 thinkingLen=43 finishReason=Some(End) usageIn=2413 usageOut=43 empty=false
[21:32:37] [ai] ← req=29 ... status=200 duration=3467ms ok=true
```

The extension UI reverted cleanly to `Draft salary answer` (no stray result, no error) — the bug is invisible from the UI; it only shows up as wasted spend in the app log.

## Suspected cause

`apps/extension/src/lib/bridge.ts`'s `cancelCurrent()` → `supersedeAnyPendingAssist()` does send an `assist.cancel` frame (`cancelAssist()`, `apps/extension/src/lib/bridge.ts:2014-2022`) and correctly stops relaying further chunks/settles the promise client-side — but nothing downstream on the desktop side appears to abort the actual provider HTTP stream for this code path. `apps/desktop/src-tauri/src/extension_bridge/answer_assist_topic.rs` (the Prep tab's on-demand `topic` extension to `answer.assist`, PR4) has no references to `cancel`/`register`/`AbortHandle`/`spawn` at all, despite its own doc comment claiming it "grounds it through the EXACT SAME draft pipeline every other `answer.assist` call uses — same gate, same `ai_research` bucket/limiter, **same registry**, same streaming frames." The real cancellable-job registry lives in `apps/desktop/src-tauri/src/extension_bridge/assist_registry.rs` (`cancel`/`cancel_all`, backed by a `JobCanceller`/`AbortHandle`) — worth confirming whether a topic-mode draft's job actually gets `register`ed into it, or whether it silently bypasses registration.

## Impact

"AI spend is real money" — a user who reflexively cancels a draft (wrong topic clicked, changed their mind, etc.) is still billed for the full generation every time, with zero indication anything went wrong.

_Found during an end-to-end test of the published 0.154.0 extension against the 0.154.0 desktop app._

title: extension: Answers-tab free-text instruction is ignored by chips and dropped server-side on Regenerate
body:
## Summary

The Answers tab's free-text "Instruction for '<question>'" box has no effect on the drafted/rewritten text, in either of the two ways a user could plausibly use it: clicking a TONE/LENGTH chip while it's filled in ignores it completely (chips carry their own hardcoded preset/instruction), and using "Regenerate"/"Draft this answer" — the one control that actually transmits the typed instruction to the desktop app — also has no effect, because the desktop's draft-mode compose path never reads the `instruction` field at all.

## Environment

extension 0.154.0 store build, desktop app 0.154.0, Windows 11, Chrome, Ollama Cloud (`gpt-oss:20b`).

## Steps to reproduce

1. Open the Answers tab on a drafted row with an existing version (e.g. "Tell us more").
2. Type a specific instruction into "Instruction for '…'", e.g. "Focus only on the websocket migration story, keep it under 120 characters total."
3a. Click a TONE or LENGTH chip (e.g. "Shorter"), OR
3b. Click "Regenerate" (the button that is documented — via the UI hint "Regenerate rethinks it from your résumé" — to be the one that uses free text).

## Expected

At least path (b) — Regenerate — incorporates the typed instruction (topic focus and/or the 120-character limit) into the new version, since it is the control that sends `instruction` in its request payload.

## Actual

Neither path reflects the instruction at all:
- (a) Chip click: result is close in length to the pre-chip text and still about React/Next.js/Tauri/etc — nothing about the requested "websocket migration" topic.
- (b) Regenerate click: result (v6, ~650 characters) still restates unrelated highlights from the résumé — no mention of "websocket" anywhere, and nowhere close to the requested 120-character limit. The desktop AI request log confirms a real, successful call was made (`req=21`, `status=200`, `duration=5663ms`) — this is not a silent failure, the instruction is simply never reaching the model.

## Root cause

- **Chips never read the free-text box.** `apps/extension/src/answer-tools/answer-tools.ts:165-190` — every `TONE_CHIPS`/`LENGTH_CHIPS` entry carries its OWN fixed `preset` or `instruction` string (e.g. `Warmer` → `"Make this warmer and more personal…"`). The click handler (`answer-tools.ts:392-401`) sends only `chip.preset`/`chip.instruction` — the view-local `instructions` map (what the user typed) is never referenced there at all.
- **Regenerate DOES send it, but the backend drops it.** `answer-tools.ts:488-503`, the Regenerate/"Draft this answer" handler, sends `mode: 'draft'` plus `instruction: instructions.get(row.id)` when non-empty (line 500) — this part is correct. But server-side, `apps/desktop/src-tauri/src/extension_bridge/answer_assist.rs`:
  - `parse_instruction`/`resolve_rewrite_instruction` (lines 388-417) are documented as "rewrite mode only" and are only invoked via `validate_rewrite_fields`, which is itself only called `match mode { AssistMode::Rewrite => Some(validate_rewrite_fields(payload)?), AssistMode::Draft => None }` (lines 720-723).
  - `build_user_message`, the draft-mode prompt builder (lines 551-592), takes `question, resume, job_description, company_brief, web_notes, salary_range` — there is no parameter for a free-text instruction anywhere in its signature or body.
  - So a `mode:'draft'` request's `instruction` field is parsed nowhere in the whole compose path; it is present on the wire and then simply never read.

## Suggested fix direction

Either wire the free-text instruction into the draft-mode prompt (extend `build_user_message` with an optional "additional instruction from the candidate" parameter, fenced the same way `question` is, and have `resolve_answer_assist`'s `AssistMode::Draft` arm read `payload.get("instruction")` and pass it through), or — if draft mode is intentionally never meant to take a free-text instruction — remove/hide the instruction box for the draft/Regenerate action (or gray it out with a note) so it isn't presented as something that shapes the next draft when it silently does nothing. The current combination (a visible, always-enabled input, a UI hint implying Regenerate is exactly the control that uses it, and total silence about the fact that nothing happens) is the misleading part.

_Found during an end-to-end test of the published 0.154.0 extension against the 0.154.0 desktop app._

title: extension: Accept into field works once per row, then fails and orphans the draft on the next Rescan
body:
## Summary

In the extension's Answers tab, "Accept into field" only works ONCE per row. After the first successful accept fills a previously-empty field, every subsequent Accept on that same row (e.g. after clicking Regenerate to produce a new version) fails immediately with "Could not find this field — the page may have changed." — even though the field is untouched, still visible, and holds exactly the text the first Accept wrote. If the user then clicks Rescan to recover, the real-world field is split into TWO panel rows: a fresh one with no draft history, and an orphaned one that keeps the AI-drafted versions but permanently loses its "Accept into field" button, stranding that work.

## Environment

extension 0.154.0 store build, desktop app 0.154.0, Windows 11, Chrome, Ollama Cloud (`gpt-oss:20b`) as the AI provider.

## Steps to reproduce

1. Open an application form with an empty text/textarea question (confirmed on Ashby, e.g. jobs.ashbyhq.com/linear/.../application, "What country are you based in?").
2. Open the side panel → Answers tab → expand that row → "Draft this answer" → "Accept into field". Confirm the page field now shows the drafted text.
3. Click "Regenerate" on the same row (produces a new version, v2/v3/…).
4. Click "Accept into field" again, without Rescanning in between.

## Expected

The new version replaces the old text in the (now non-empty) field, the same way "Accept" worked the first time.

## Actual

Step 4 fails instantly: `"Could not find this field — the page may have changed."` The field itself is confirmed present and unchanged (verified by reading the live DOM value directly: still holds exactly what the first Accept wrote). Reproduced 1/1 cleanly; the message is actively misleading since nothing about the page changed.

If the user then clicks **Rescan** to try to recover: the Answers tab count inflates (4 questions → 5 in my repro) and the SAME real field now shows as two separate rows — one labelled "…Filled" with no version history (Accept works fine on this one), and the original row (still showing its full v1..vN draft history) with NO "Accept into field" button at all — only Copy/Regenerate remain, so the user's edited draft can never be written to the page again without manually copy-pasting it themselves.

## Root cause

- `writeRowText` (`apps/extension/src/background.ts:1954-1988`) branches on `row.field.kind` ('empty' vs 'filled') to pick `injectAnswerFill` (empty-field path) vs `injectAnswerReplace` (filled-field path). On a successful write, its state update (lines 1979-1986) only refreshes `field.currentText` — it never flips `field.kind` from `'empty'` to `'filled'`.
- So a second Accept on the same row still takes the `injectAnswerFill` branch, which calls `locateQuestionField` (`apps/extension/src/lib/answers-capture.ts:247-256`) — this only searches `emptyCandidateFields`. Since the field is no longer empty, it is absent from that candidate set, the occurrence count no longer matches, and the function returns `null` → the fixed `NOT_FOUND` result (`apps/extension/src/lib/answer-fill.ts:44-47`), surfaced verbatim as "Could not find this field — the page may have changed."
- The Rescan-time row-split is a direct consequence: `fieldRowId(kind, question, index)` (`apps/extension/src/lib/answer-state.ts:197-199`) bakes `kind` into the row's own id. A fresh scan of the now-genuinely-filled field produces a `filled:…` id, which is different from the original `empty:…` id the row was created under, so `buildRows`'s carry-over-by-id logic (`answer-state.ts:254-332`) cannot reunite them — it creates a brand-new "Filled" row for the live field and leaves the old row to survive only because it "holds versions" (per that function's own doc comment), now with `field` undefined and therefore no Accept action (`canAccept`, gating `apps/extension/src/answer-tools/answer-tools.ts:459`).

## Suggested fix direction

When `writeRowText` succeeds against an `'empty'`-kind field, also flip `field.kind` to `'filled'` in the same state update (alongside `currentText`) so a second Accept correctly takes the `injectAnswerReplace` path without needing a Rescan. Separately, `buildRows`'s carry-over might consider matching a prior row by `(question, index)` ignoring `kind` when the exact-id match misses (or the field ref could migrate to `filled:...`'s row rather than orphaning the original), so a Rescan doesn't strand drafted versions were the kind-transition to happen anyway.

_Found during an end-to-end test of the published 0.154.0 extension against the 0.154.0 desktop app._

title: extension: side panel trust line renders the agent `job` resource's literal `<job_posting>` prompt-fence wrapper instead of stripping it for display
body:
## Summary

The extension's side panel "Reading: …" trust line, and the `ajh-tauri agent job <url>` CLI output, both show the literal `<job_posting>…</job_posting>` prompt-injection-defense wrapper around a tracked job's `title`/`company` (and, on the CLI, `location`/`description`) instead of plain text. The wrapper is intentional and transient — applied only when a value crosses the agent/MCP read boundary (ADR-010) — but the extension's own human-facing UI reuses that exact boundary for its own display and never strips the markup back off, so a security artifact meant only for an LLM prompt leaks into text a person reads.

This does **not** indicate any corruption of the desktop's stored job data — see "What this is not," below.

## Environment

extension 0.154.0, desktop app 0.154.0, Windows 11, Chrome.

## Steps to reproduce

1. Have autopilot track at least one job (any board).
2. Open the extension's side panel on that job's own tab, or run `ajh-tauri agent job "<a tracked job's url>"` from the CLI.
3. Read the panel's trust line, or the CLI's `title`/`company`/`location`/`description` fields.

## Expected

The `job` agent-read resource's fence wrapper exists for an AI/MCP consumer building a model prompt (`apps/desktop/src-tauri/src/extension_bridge/agent_read.rs`'s own doc: "a consumer whose entire purpose is 'an AI agent reads this'"). A human-facing renderer — the side panel's trust line — should strip that wrapper (or the extension should have its own small unwrap helper) before display.

## Actual

Both the CLI reply and the side panel's trust line show the literal `<job_posting>`/`</job_posting>` tags wrapped around `title`/`company` (CLI also shows them on `location`/`description`).

## Root cause

- `apps/desktop/src-tauri/src/extension_bridge/agent_read.rs:605-611` (`fence_description`) and `apps/desktop/src-tauri/src/extension_bridge/agent_read/best_matches.rs:256-264` (`fence_posting_display_fields`) wrap `description` and `title`/`company`/`location` respectively, unconditionally, on every `job` resource reply — by design (ADR-010), and this never mutates the underlying store.
- `apps/extension/src/background.ts:700-706` (`readJobTitleCompany`) and `apps/extension/src/background.ts:716-723` (`runTrustLineJob`) call `agentQuery('job', {url})` and copy `title`/`company` out of the reply as-is, with no fence-stripping.
- `apps/extension/src/sidepanel/sidepanel.ts:302-312` (`refreshTrustLineJob`) then renders `Reading: ${res.title} · ${res.company}` with the wrapper markup still attached.
- `rg -n "job_posting" apps/extension/src` (excluding tests) returns no hits — the extension's TypeScript has no code anywhere that knows about or strips this fence-tag convention.

## Suggested fix direction

Add a small client-side unwrap helper in the extension (mirroring `prompt_fence::strip_fence_wrapper`'s exact-shape match: strip a `<job_posting>\n…\n</job_posting>` wrapper only when the string matches that precise shape) and apply it wherever the extension displays a `title`/`company`/`location`/`description` value read through `agent.query`'s `job` (and likely `best-matches`/`found-jobs`) resource, starting with `readJobTitleCompany` in `apps/extension/src/background.ts`.

## Note: what this is not

An earlier version of this issue attributed the same visible symptom to the desktop *persisting* fence tags into the found-jobs/autopilot store via a write path that supposedly lacked `unfence_job_field`'s protection (`apps/desktop/src-tauri/src/prompt_fence.rs:478`, applied in `apps/desktop/src-tauri/src/commands/scrape.rs:532-548`). That is not what happens: the only writer of `FoundJob`'s text fields, `build_found_job` (`apps/desktop/src-tauri/src/commands/autopilot.rs:900-918`), copies them straight from the raw scraped posting, and no agent-reachable write command exposes an individual found job's fields for write at all (`autopilot_update`'s schema, `packages/shared/src/schemas/index.ts:981-983`, only edits autopilot-level config). The wrapper is applied fresh, transiently, on every `job` resource read — exactly as designed — and the only real defect is that the extension's own display code doesn't undo it before showing the text to a person.

title: extension: Attach always reports "more than one résumé field" on Greenhouse-style forms with a separate cover-letter upload
body:
## Summary
`isResumeFileInput`'s fallback rule matches a file input as "résumé-like" when its `accept` attribute lists document types (`pdf|\.docx?|msword|wordprocessingml`), with no requirement that the name/id/label also mention résumé/CV. On a very common real-world ATS pattern — a separate, optional "Cover Letter" file upload sitting next to the "Resume/CV" upload, both accepting the same document types — this fallback matches BOTH inputs, so Attach always reports "Found more than one résumé upload field on this page — attach it yourself," even though the correct field is trivially identifiable by its id/name alone.

## Environment
Extension 0.154.0 (store build), desktop app 0.154.0, Windows 11, Chrome. Reproduced on a real Greenhouse application form (`job-boards.greenhouse.io`).

## Steps to reproduce
1. Open a Greenhouse job application page that has both a résumé upload and a separate cover-letter upload.
2. Open the side panel's Documents tab, pick a résumé source, and click "Attach résumé to this page".

## Expected
Attach locates the résumé-specific field and attaches to it (its `id="resume"` is unambiguous).

## Actual
`"Found more than one résumé upload field on this page — attach it yourself."` — reproduced 3/3 tries (deterministic, not flaky). DOM inspection of the two file inputs:
```json
[{"id":"resume","accept":".pdf,.doc,.docx,.txt,.rtf"},
 {"id":"cover_letter","accept":".pdf,.doc,.docx,.txt,.rtf"}]
```
Both inputs share the exact same `accept` list, so both match `RESUME_FILE_ACCEPT_RE`, and neither `id` needed to say "resume" for the false match — the `cover_letter` field matched purely on `accept`.

## Root cause
`apps/extension/src/lib/submit-watch.ts:110-131`:
```ts
const RESUME_FILE_TEXT_RE = /resume|curriculum|lebenslauf|(?:^|[^a-z])cv/;
const RESUME_FILE_ACCEPT_RE = /pdf|\.docx?|msword|wordprocessingml/;
...
return RESUME_FILE_TEXT_RE.test(textSignal(el)) || RESUME_FILE_ACCEPT_RE.test(accept);
```
The two signals are OR'd with no way for one to disambiguate the other, and the `accept`-only match is too generic — "accepts a PDF or Word doc" is true of nearly every document upload field on a job application form, résumé or not.

## Suggested fix direction
When the accept-based match alone would produce more than one candidate on the page, prefer any candidate whose name/id/label/aria-label matches `RESUME_FILE_TEXT_RE`, and/or explicitly exclude a field whose text signal matches a cover-letter pattern (`cover.?letter|anschreiben|motivation`) even if its `accept` list matches.

_Found during an end-to-end test of the published 0.154.0 extension's Documents tab against the 0.154.0 desktop app._

title: extension: popup's Fill has no first-time confirmation at all, unlike the identical side-panel action
body:
## Summary
"Fill this form" exists in both the popup (`popup.html`) and the side panel's Job tab, calling the same underlying `fill` action — but only the side panel wires a `confirmFill` dependency into `mountJobTools`. The popup passes no `confirmFill` at all, so clicking Fill from the popup fires immediately with zero confirmation, on any host, even the very first time. The side panel shows the "First Fill on `<host>`" dialog for the identical action on the identical host.

## Environment
Extension 0.154.0 (store build), desktop app 0.154.0, Windows 11, Chrome.

## Steps to reproduce
1. Pick a job application form on a host that has never been confirmed (`fillConfirmDontAskHosts` empty for it).
2. Trigger the extension's toolbar button to open the popup, and click "Fill this form".
3. Separately (fresh host), open the side panel's Job tab and click "Fill this form" there.

## Expected
Consistent trust gating for the same destructive-ish action (it writes into a live application form) regardless of which surface triggered it.

## Actual
- Popup: click → immediately "Filled 6 fields — review them on the page (name split is a guess — verify)." — no dialog shown at all.
- Panel, same host reset to unconfirmed: click → "FIRST FILL ON `<HOST>`" dialog appears first, requiring an explicit "Fill" click (or "Don't ask again") before anything is filled.

## Root cause
- `apps/extension/src/popup/popup.ts:169` — `mountJobTools(els.jobToolsHost, { send, hideSaveAnswers: true })` — no `confirmFill`.
- `apps/extension/src/sidepanel/sidepanel.ts:215-233` — `mountJobTools(jobToolsHost, { send, confirmFill: async () => { ... } })` — wires the dialog.

## Suggested fix direction
Either give the popup the same `confirmFill` wiring (with its own small inline confirm, since the popup has no persistent side-panel-style inset to reuse), or make the first-Fill trust decision live somewhere both surfaces read from before calling `fill`, so the guarantee "you'll be asked before your saved details are written into a form for the first time on this site" holds regardless of entry point.

_Found during an end-to-end test of the published 0.154.0 extension against the 0.154.0 desktop app._

title: extension: Fill's first-time confirmation dialog claims it fills the résumé file, but Fill never touches file inputs
body:
## Summary
The first-time Fill confirmation dialog's copy says "This will fill: name, email, phone, résumé file." — but Fill's `FILLABLE_TYPES` only ever fills `text | email | tel | url` inputs and explicitly excludes `type=file`. Fill can never attach a résumé file; that's what the separate Documents-tab "Attach" action is for. The confirmation the user is asked to approve overstates what the action will actually do.

## Environment
Extension 0.154.0 (store build), desktop app 0.154.0, Windows 11, Chrome. Reproduced on a real Greenhouse application form.

## Steps to reproduce
1. Open the side panel on a job application page with a résumé file-upload field, on a host that has never been confirmed.
2. Click "Fill this form" in the Job tab.
3. Read the confirmation dialog copy, then click Fill and check the file input afterward.

## Expected
The dialog only promises what Fill actually does (name/email/phone-type text fields).

## Actual
Dialog text: `"This will fill: name, email, phone, résumé file. Nothing is submitted — you review and press the site's own button."`
After confirming and filling, the page's `resume` and `cover_letter` file inputs were both still empty (`files.length === 0`) — Fill filled 6 text/email/tel fields (first name, last name, email, phone, location, LinkedIn) and never touched either file input, as expected from the code. The dialog's "résumé file" claim never happens via this action.

## Root cause
- `apps/extension/src/lib/site-memory.ts` — `DEFAULT_FILL_CONFIRM_COPY` includes "…résumé file."
- `apps/extension/src/lib/autofill.ts:111` — `FILLABLE_TYPES` (`text | email | tel | url`) has no `file` entry; file inputs are never candidates for Fill.

## Suggested fix direction
Drop "résumé file" from `DEFAULT_FILL_CONFIRM_COPY`, or split it into two distinct sentences/dialogs if the intent is eventually to also mention that a separate Attach action exists for the résumé file.

_Found during an end-to-end test of the published 0.154.0 extension against the 0.154.0 desktop app._

title: extension: Documents tab shows permanent "Loading…" instead of the Job tab's "grant access" message when the page isn't trusted
body:
## Summary
When the followed tab is not "trusted" (`isPageTrusted(state)` false — the same condition that makes the Job tab show its clear "Click the toolbar icon to grant access to this page, then use these tools." line), the side panel calls `documents.reset()` instead of `documents.refresh()`. `reset()` clears the candidate list and sets an EMPTY status text, and the Documents tab's render function falls back to the literal placeholder string `"Loading…"` whenever there are no candidates and no explicit status. The result: the Documents tab shows "Loading…" forever — not because anything is in flight, but because the page isn't trusted — with no error, no explanation, and no visible way to recover, while the Job tab (driven by the exact same state) shows a clear, actionable message for the identical condition.

## Environment
Extension 0.154.0 (store build), desktop app 0.154.0, Windows 11, Chrome.

## Steps to reproduce
1. Open the side panel already following some tab.
2. Navigate that same tab to a different site (a plain in-tab navigation, no toolbar click).
3. Open/stay on the Documents tab.

## Expected
Either the doc list loads, or — matching the Job tab's behaviour for the identical untrusted state — a clear message telling the user to click the toolbar icon.

## Actual
The Documents tab is stuck on "Loading…" indefinitely (observed for 2+ minutes with zero backend activity and zero console output) while the Job tab, showing the SAME follow() state, correctly renders "Click the toolbar icon to grant access to this page, then use these tools." Reproduced on 2 separate hosts (an Ashby direct-application page and a happyhotel/Ashby iframe-embedded page) after an ordinary same-tab navigation — no rapid tab-cycling needed.

Confirmed the message channel itself is fine: calling the exact same request manually from the panel's own context resolves instantly —
```js
await chrome.runtime.sendMessage({kind:'documentsList'})
// => {"ok":true,"kind":"documentsList","result":{"ok":false,"resource":"documents","error":"url is required"},"url":""}
```
— so a real (if itself imperfect — see below) response exists in under a second; the Documents tab component just never gets a chance to render it because `refresh()` was never called for this state in the first place.

## Root cause
- `apps/extension/src/sidepanel/sidepanel.ts:403-417` (inside `follow()`'s `subscribeAnswerState` callback): `documents.refresh()` is only called at line 408, inside the `if (state && isPageTrusted(state))` branch. The `else` branch (lines 410-414) calls `documents.reset()` instead, which never triggers a fetch.
- `apps/extension/src/documents/documents.ts:557-565` (`reset()`): sets `setStatus('', 'muted')` — an empty status — then renders.
- `apps/extension/src/documents/documents.ts` (render, ~line 216): `host.append(el('p', 'msg msg--muted', statusText || 'Loading…'))` — an empty status text falls back to the literal string "Loading…", indistinguishable from a genuine in-flight fetch.

As a secondary, related issue: `runDocumentsList()` (`apps/extension/src/background.ts:795-799`) resolves the active tab's URL via `browser.tabs.query({active:true, currentWindow:true}).catch(() => '')`; in the panel context this can itself resolve to an empty string (`tab?.url` empty), producing the Rust side's `"url is required"` error shown above — but that response is moot here since the panel never calls `refresh()` for the untrusted state to begin with.

## Suggested fix direction
Give the Documents tab (and Prep, which has the identical `else` branch at sidepanel.ts:414) a distinct "page not trusted / click the toolbar icon" status instead of a silent `reset()`, mirroring the Job tab's gated line — e.g. have `reset()` accept an explicit reason/status string, or have `follow()` pass the untrusted state through so `documents.render(state)` can show it.

_Found during an end-to-end test of the published 0.154.0 extension's Documents tab against the 0.154.0 desktop app._

title: extension: Attach's first-time confirmation dialog is invisible when clicked from the Documents tab (silent hang)
body:
## Summary The Documents tab's "Attach résumé to this page" button uses the SAME first-time-per-host confirmation dialog as the Job tab's "Fill this form" (`mountFirstFillConfirm`), but that dialog is DOM-mounted inside the Job tab's `
`. Since the tab bar hides inactive tab panels with the `hidden` attribute, clicking Attach while the Documents tab is the active tab renders the confirmation dialog inside a `hidden` ancestor — fully built (correct copy, buttons, checkbox) but completely invisible and unclickable. The `await fillConfirm.confirm(...)` call the click handler is waiting on has no way to ever resolve, so the whole Attach action just hangs forever with zero feedback. ## Environment Extension 0.154.0 (store build), desktop app 0.154.0, Windows 11, Chrome. Reproduced on a real Greenhouse application page (`job-boards.greenhouse.io`). ## Steps to reproduce 1. Open the side panel on a job page whose host has never been confirmed for Fill/Attach (`fillConfirmDontAskHosts` has no entry for it). 2. Switch to the Documents tab (never visit the Job tab first). 3. Click "Attach résumé to this page". ## Expected Either the same "First Attach on ``" confirmation dialog the Job tab shows, or at minimum a visible response of some kind. ## Actual Nothing happens. The button just gets focus; no dialog, no status message, no console error, no network/bridge activity. It looks completely broken. Reproduced 2/2 tries. Switching to the Job tab afterward reveals the pending "FIRST ATTACH ON ``" dialog that was silently waiting there the whole time — proving the click was accepted and is hung, not ignored. ## Evidence `evaluate_script` on the side panel while the Documents tab was active: ```json {"jobPanelHidden": true, "docPanelHidden": false, "jobPanelChildCount": 4, "jobPanelInnerHTMLTail": "...

First Attach on

This will attach your résumé file — nothing is submitted.

..."} ``` The dialog markup exists, fully rendered with the right host and copy, inside `jobPanel` while `jobPanelHidden: true`. ## Root cause - `apps/extension/src/sidepanel/sidepanel.ts:185-187`: `fillConfirmHost` is created and appended to `jobPanel` (the Job tab's section), and `mountFirstFillConfirm` is mounted there once. - `apps/extension/src/sidepanel/sidepanel.ts:241`: the Documents tab's `confirmAttach` reuses that exact same `fillConfirm.confirm(...)` instance/DOM host — there is no separate mount for Documents. - `apps/extension/src/tabs/tabs.ts:82-89` (`setActive`): `entry.panel.hidden = !active` — the Job tab's `
` gets `hidden = true` whenever any other tab is selected, and `hidden` cascades to all descendants regardless of their own `hidden` state, so the confirmation dialog is unreachable by the user. ## Suggested fix direction Mount `fillConfirmHost` outside the tab bar's hidden `
` panels entirely (e.g. as a sibling overlay at the top level of the side panel), so it stays visible/interactive no matter which tab is currently selected. _Found during an end-to-end test of the published 0.154.0 extension's Documents tab against the 0.154.0 desktop app._

title: Check fit: missing-keyword chips can include non-job-content junk (nav/chart text), score shifted once on an unchanged posting
body:
## Summary

"Check fit"'s "missing keywords" chips (the "why?" disclosure) can be populated with tokens that are clearly not job-posting vocabulary — URL path fragments and job-board chart-widget date labels — rather than genuine skills/requirements the résumé lacks. On the same, completely unchanged posting, the fit score itself also shifted once (27% → 21%, then stayed stable at 21% across 6 further repeated clicks), which is consistent with the extracted job text not being fully stable across capture attempts.

## Environment

Extension 0.154.0 (store build == repo main), desktop app 0.154.0, Windows 11, Chrome. LinkedIn job posting (`linkedin.com/jobs/view/...` and the equivalent job-search detail pane).

## Steps to reproduce

1. Open a LinkedIn job posting (one with a company "Hiring insights" panel — employee-growth chart, applicant-education/seniority stats — which LinkedIn shows on most postings).
2. Click "Check fit" immediately after the page/pane finishes loading, and expand "why?".
3. Click "Check fit" again a few more times on the same, unreloaded tab/posting.

## Expected

Missing-keyword chips should be job-relevant terms genuinely present in the posting text but absent from the résumé. The score should be identical across repeated calls on the same, unchanged posting and résumé.

## Actual

- Chips observed for one real posting (Harvey, "Staff Software Engineer, Frontend"): `/company/harvey`, `1sep`, `2025mar`, `2026sep`, `accommodations` — the first four are clearly not job-posting keywords (a link path fragment and what look like abbreviated chart axis date labels from the "Hiring insights" employee-growth chart on the same page), not skills or requirements text.
- The FIRST "Check fit" call (via the popup, right after the page/pane finished loading) scored this posting 27%. Every subsequent call on the exact same tab/posting/résumé (6 more clicks, via both popup and panel) consistently scored it 21% — a real, reproducible one-time shift, not click-to-click noise (it never moved again after the first call).

## Evidence

- Screenshots: expanded "why?" chip list showing `/company/harvey`, `1sep`, `2025mar`, `2026sep`, `accommodations`, immediately followed by the correct "Posting says $231,000 - $340,000" line (so the surrounding extraction IS finding the real posting — the junk is additive, not a wrong-page capture).
- Score sequence recorded across 7 consecutive "Check fit" clicks on the one tab (no reload between any of them): 27%, then 21%, 21%, 21%, 21%, 21%, 21%.

## Root cause (repo-relative path:line refs, best available from static reading — not fully confirmed against the LinkedIn DOM itself)

- `apps/desktop/src-tauri/src/commands/match_resume.rs:366-399` computes `job_keywords`/`gaps` directly from `job_text`, with no filtering beyond stopwords/stemming — whatever text arrives in `job_text` becomes candidate "missing keyword" material verbatim.
- `job_text` traces back to the `description` field `apps/desktop/src-tauri/src/scraping/scrape_url/mod.rs:466-548` (`parse_from_html`) assembles for the extension's Scan-mode capture, via JSON-LD → `data-ajh-job-root` hint → `readability_content_text`/`main_content_text` fallback (`mod.rs:540-548`). The specific chip content (a chart's date-axis labels, a nav-link path) is consistent with page chrome outside the actual job-description block leaking into whichever of those extraction paths ran for this capture — LinkedIn's SPA is a plausible case where the hint/JSON-LD may not scope as tightly as a fully server-rendered page.

## Suggested fix direction

Filter/validate candidate keyword tokens before they can surface as "missing keyword" chips — e.g. reject tokens that are pure digit/month-abbreviation runs or contain path-separator characters — as a defensive floor independent of fixing the upstream extraction scoping. Separately, worth double-checking whether `job_text` capture/extraction is fully deterministic for an unchanged LinkedIn posting, since the score itself moved once in this session.

_Found during an end-to-end test of the published 0.154.0 extension against the 0.154.0 desktop app. Lower confidence than the other findings from this track — flagging for the owning domain expert to confirm the exact leak point._

title: Check fit: German trailing-currency-symbol salary ("60.000 € – 75.000 €") never detected
body:
## Summary

"Check fit"'s salary-fact extraction (`salary.posting`, shown as "Posting says …" in the popup/panel/on-page badge) requires a currency symbol or ISO code to come BEFORE the first number of a range. German job postings very commonly write amounts with the currency symbol AFTER each number instead ("60.000 € – 75.000 €"), which never matches. The UI then shows no salary line at all — identical to a posting that genuinely lists no salary — even though the page states one clearly.

## Environment

Extension 0.154.0 (store build == repo main), desktop app 0.154.0, Windows 11, Chrome.

## Steps to reproduce

1. Open (or view) a German job posting that states its salary as "NN.NNN € – NN.NNN €" (symbol trailing each number, which is the common convention on German job boards, vs. the leading-symbol convention on English-language/US boards).
2. Click "Check fit" and expand "why?" in the result card.

## Expected

The card should show a "Posting says 60.000 € – 75.000 €" line, the same way it shows "Posting says $231,000 - $340,000" for a US posting with symbol-first phrasing.

## Actual

No salary line appears anywhere in the result (popup, panel, or on-page badge) — the UI is indistinguishable from a posting that has no salary information at all. Reproduced twice with a minimal, realistic posting page containing exactly the line "Je nach Erfahrung bieten wir ein Jahresgehalt von 60.000 € – 75.000 € brutto." (a 50%-match posting, so the fit card rendered normally, just with no salary fact).

## Evidence

- Screenshot: the expanded "why?" panel for this posting shows missing-keyword chips ("entwickler", "m/w/d", "testjobsde") and "Résumé used: …" but no "Posting says …" line, despite the page's own text containing an unambiguous, correctly-formatted salary range.
- For comparison, the SAME session correctly extracted and displayed "Posting says $231,000 - $340,000" for a US LinkedIn posting phrased with the symbol first ("$231,000 - $340,000"), confirming the regex itself works — only the trailing-symbol phrasing is missed.

## Root cause (repo-relative path:line refs)

- `apps/desktop/src-tauri/src/extraction/salary.rs:28` (`CURRENCY`) and `:42-47` (`SALARY_RANGE_RE`) build the pattern as `{CURRENCY}\s*{NUMBER}\s*{SEPARATOR}\s*{CURRENCY}?\s*{NUMBER}` — the currency marker is REQUIRED immediately before the FIRST number (only the second occurrence is optional). A string where the currency symbol instead follows each number ("60.000 € – 75.000 €") never satisfies the leading `{CURRENCY}` before the first `{NUMBER}`, so the whole match fails and `extract_salary_range` (`salary.rs:94-96`) returns `None`.
- The UI has no distinct "salary present but unparsed" state — `salary.posting` being absent renders identically whether the posting truly has no salary or the extractor simply missed a real one, so there is no way for a user to tell these apart from the fit card alone.

## Suggested fix direction

Add a second pattern (or make the marker's position symmetric) that also matches a NUMBER immediately followed by the CURRENCY marker, so `NN.NNN €` phrasing matches on either side, while keeping the "always require a currency marker somewhere" discipline that already excludes bare number ranges / dates / percentages.

title: On-page fit badge goes stale after an in-page SPA job-to-job navigation
body:
## Summary

The on-page fit badge ("AI Job Hunter fit: N% — ...") that "Check fit" paints in the bottom-right corner of a job posting is never cleared or refreshed when the user moves to a DIFFERENT posting via a client-side (SPA) navigation, such as selecting another card in LinkedIn's job-search results without a full page reload. The badge keeps showing the FIRST posting's score, résumé match, and missing-keyword chips while the visible page has completely changed to a different job.

## Environment

Extension 0.154.0 (store build == repo main), desktop app 0.154.0, Windows 11, Chrome. LinkedIn job-search results (`linkedin.com/jobs/search/...`), which routes card selection client-side without a full navigation.

## Steps to reproduce

1. On a LinkedIn job-search results page, open the popup on the first result and click "Check fit". The on-page badge appears bottom-right with that posting's score (e.g. "27% low match").
2. Without reloading, click a DIFFERENT job card in the results list on the left. LinkedIn updates the URL's `currentJobId`, the page's `<h1>`/company/description, and the whole right-hand detail pane to the new posting — client-side, no navigation event the extension listens for.
3. Look at the on-page badge again.

## Expected

The badge should disappear (or at least clearly indicate it no longer matches what's on screen) once the user is looking at a different posting than the one it was computed for.

## Actual

The badge is still present, unchanged, still showing the FIRST posting's exact score/band/résumé-name/missing-keywords, now overlaid on a completely different job's page. Nothing in the UI hints that the number is stale. Reproduced 2/2 tries (tested Harvey → Suno, and again after re-checking Harvey).

## Evidence

- Screenshots: before navigation, `<h1>` = "Staff Software Engineer, Frontend" (Harvey), badge = "27% low match"; after clicking the Suno card (no reload), `<h1>` = "Senior / Staff Software Engineer, Frontend" (Suno), URL `currentJobId` changed from `4432888947` to `4463942585`, badge STILL reads "27% low match" (Harvey's number).
- Confirmed via `document.getElementById('ajh-fit-badge')` still present with the same content both before and after the SPA navigation — the host node is never removed or repainted.

## Root cause (repo-relative path:line refs)

- `apps/extension/src/background.ts:1341-1361` (`injectFitBadge`) only guards against painting the badge for the WRONG posting on arrival (`if (location.href !== expectedUrl) return;` at `background.ts:1346`) — it never runs again to re-check or clear an EXISTING badge once the tab's own URL changes later.
- `apps/extension/src/background.ts:2432-2437` (`browser.tabs.onUpdated` listener) only reacts `if (changeInfo.status !== 'loading')`, i.e. to real navigations. LinkedIn's job-to-job card selection is a same-document `history.pushState`/`replaceState` update, which Chrome does not reliably surface through `tabs.onUpdated` the same way — so nothing in the background script ever learns the user moved to a different posting and nothing calls back into the content script to remove `#ajh-fit-badge`.
- The badge is only ever cleared as a side effect of a NEW successful "Check fit" call repainting it (`apps/extension/src/lib/fit-badge.ts:74`, "always clears any prior badge first") — there is no independent navigation-driven cleanup path.

## Suggested fix direction

Have the content-script side that owns the badge also watch for same-document navigation (e.g. wrap `history.pushState`/`replaceState`, or poll `location.href` on a short interval / `MutationObserver` on the title) and remove `#ajh-fit-badge` as soon as the URL changes out from under it, independent of whether a new "Check fit" ever gets triggered for the new posting.

title: Stamp results page: duplicate Saved/Applied pills accumulate on repeated Stamp clicks
body:
## Summary

"Stamp this results page" places a "Saved"/"Applied" pill next to each matched job card by appending a new host element after the card's anchor. The de-dup guard that is supposed to remove a card's previous stamp before placing a new one lives in module-level `WeakMap`s inside `results-stamp.ts` — but that file is injected as a fresh classic script on every single "Stamp" click, so the guard's memory is empty every time even though the DOM nodes from earlier clicks are still sitting on the page. Result: every repeated "Stamp this results page" click on an unchanged results page adds one more duplicate pill to the same card instead of replacing the existing one.

## Environment

Extension 0.154.0 (store build == repo main), desktop app 0.154.0, Windows 11, Chrome.

## Steps to reproduce

1. Open a job board's listing page that has at least one card the desktop app already has tracked (saved/applied) — e.g. a Greenhouse company board (`job-boards.greenhouse.io/<company>`) with one already-imported posting.
2. Open the extension popup (or panel) and click "Stamp this results page". Confirm the status reads "Stamped 1 card." and exactly one "Saved ×" pill appears next to the tracked card.
3. Without reloading or navigating, click "Stamp this results page" again on the same page.

## Expected

The second click should leave exactly one pill on the card (replace, not add), since nothing about the page or the tracked posting changed between clicks.

## Actual

The second click adds a SECOND identical "Saved ×" pill next to the same card, both fully interactive (each with its own working dismiss "×"). Reproduced 2/2 tries in a row; each further click would add another.

## Evidence

- Screenshots: `apps/extension` evidence captured during this test — one card ("Engineering Manager — Premium Cards (Frontend)" on `job-boards.greenhouse.io/dkbcodefactory`) with exactly one "Saved ×" pill after the first Stamp click, and the same card with two "Saved ×" pills side by side after the second Stamp click on the same, unreloaded page. No other card on the board (including the adjacent, similarly-named "Premium Cards (Mobile)" card) ever gets a pill — targeting itself is correct, only the re-run dedup is broken.

## Root cause (repo-relative path:line refs)

- `apps/extension/src/lib/results-stamp.ts:64,69` — `stampNodes`/`stampShadows` are plain module-level `WeakMap`s, the ONLY bookkeeping `placeStamp` (`results-stamp.ts:137-182`) has for "did I already stamp this anchor".
- `apps/extension/src/lib/results-stamp.ts:143` (`placeStamp` calls `clearStamp(anchor)` first) and `results-stamp.ts:121-125` (`clearStamp` looks the anchor up in `stampNodes`/`stampShadows` before removing anything) — this only works if the maps still hold the entry from the PREVIOUS run.
- `apps/extension/src/background.ts:974` — `runStampResults` injects `results-stamp.js` via `browser.scripting.executeScript({ target: { tabId }, files: ['results-stamp.js'] })` on every single "Stamp" click. Chrome re-executes a classic script's top-level code on each injection, so `stampNodes`/`stampShadows` are re-declared as brand-new EMPTY maps every time — `clearStamp` can never find a stamp placed by an earlier injection, even though that stamp's actual DOM node (`results-stamp.ts:145-179`, `anchor.insertAdjacentElement('afterend', host)`) is still physically in the page.

## Suggested fix direction

Make the dedup check DOM-based instead of (or in addition to) memory-based: before inserting a new host, look for an existing `[data-ajh-stamp]` sibling right after the anchor (`anchor.nextElementSibling?.matches('[data-ajh-stamp="true"]')`) and remove/replace it, since that check survives a fresh script injection the same way the DOM itself does.

title: extension: check-fit's reload advice is wrong on Web Store and PDF-viewer pages
body:
## Summary
Clicking "Check fit" on a page Chrome permanently blocks from content-script access (e.g. the Chrome Web Store) or whose rendered content the desktop app can never turn into job text (Chrome's built-in PDF viewer) shows an error message telling the user to reload the page. Reloading never helps in either case — the failure is structural, not transient — so the message gives actionable-sounding advice that cannot work.

## Environment
extension 0.154.0 store build, desktop app 0.154.0, Windows 11, Chrome

## Steps to reproduce
1. Open the extension popup on a Chrome Web Store page (`chromewebstore.google.com/...`) and click "Check fit".
2. Separately, open a PDF that Chrome renders in its built-in viewer and click "Check fit" in the popup.

## Expected
Since Chrome permanently disallows content-script injection on the Web Store, and its native PDF viewer exposes no extractable job-posting text, the failure message should not suggest that reloading will fix it.

## Actual
- Chrome Web Store: "Could not read this page. Reload the job page and try again."
- PDF viewer: "Could not read this job posting. Reload the page and try again."

Two different fixed strings for what is functionally the same class of failure (a page that can never be scripted or parsed), both implying reload is a fix. Reproduced consistently on both page types.

## Evidence
- "Could not read this page. Reload the job page and try again." — shown when the content-script capture itself fails.
- "Could not read this job posting. Reload the page and try again." — shown when capture succeeds but no job text can be extracted server-side; forwarded to the popup unchanged.

## Root cause
- `apps/extension/src/background.ts:1406-1423` (`runMatchLive`) always returns the fixed "reload the job page" text on any `captureTabHtml` failure, with no check for hosts Chrome permanently excludes from scripting.
- `apps/desktop/src-tauri/src/extension_bridge/match_live.rs:89-95,286-297` (`NO_JOB_TEXT_MESSAGE`) always suggests reload when no job text can be extracted, even for a page (PDF viewer) that will produce the same empty result on every reload.
- `apps/extension/src/job-tools/job-tools.ts:239-245` (`resolveMatchLiveResponse`) forwards both server- and client-side messages to the popup verbatim, with no distinction for permanently-restricted page types.

## Suggested fix direction
Before capturing, check the active tab's URL against Chrome's known permanently-restricted patterns (`chrome://`, `chrome-extension://`, `https://chromewebstore.google.com/*`, the built-in PDF viewer) and short-circuit with wording that says the page can't be read here, rather than suggesting a reload; keep the existing "reload and try again" copy only for failures that are plausibly transient.

title: extension: X/Twitter link fields are captured as AI-draftable Answers questions
body:
## Summary

The Answers-tab field matcher only recognizes LinkedIn, GitHub, and portfolio/website links as identity/link fields. Any other social-link field — for example a bare "X" label for a Twitter/X profile handle — falls through every exclusion gate unrecognized and is captured as a genuine, AI-draftable application question, with the full tone/length/regenerate "Draft this answer" UI, on a field that is really just a handle or URL.

## Environment

extension 0.154.0 (store build), desktop app 0.154.0, Windows 11, Chrome

## Steps to reproduce

1. Open an ATS application form (confirmed on Ashby) that has GitHub, LinkedIn, and X (Twitter) profile-link fields.
2. Open the extension side panel → Answers tab → Rescan.
3. Expand the row whose label is exactly "X".

## Expected

The X field is recognized as an identity/link field and excluded from the Answers question list, the same way the GitHub and LinkedIn fields on the same form already are — or, at minimum, it is not offered the full AI-drafting treatment, since there's nothing to compose.

## Actual

The field labelled "X" is captured as a full question, with TONE (Warmer/Formal/Simpler/…) and LENGTH chips and a "Draft this answer" button — identical to a genuine essay question like "Tell us more". Reproduced on 2/2 scans of the same form (initial scan and after Rescan).

## Root cause

- `apps/extension/src/lib/field-signal.ts`'s `NAMED_KEY_PATTERNS` table (~line 528) maps only `linkedin`, `github`, and `website` (portfolio/personal site) to a recognized identity key — there is no `twitter`/`x` pattern.
- The `AMBIGUOUS` denylist and its siblings (`field-signal.ts`, ~lines 34-223) have no protection for a bare "X"/"twitter" token either; a bare `x` can't safely be added as an unanchored substring (it would match "experience", "text", "next", etc.) — it needs a `\b`-anchored entry, the same technique already used for other short tokens in `AMBIGUOUS_WORDS`.
- `apps/extension/src/lib/answers-capture.ts`'s `isCapturable` (~line 95) only excludes a field via `matchAutocompleteKey`, `isAmbiguousSignal`, or `matchNamedKey`; none of those fire for a bare "X" label, and the ATS renders the field as a plain `type=text` input, so `CAPTURABLE_INPUT_TYPES` (~line 82) doesn't filter it either.
- This isn't a case of an existing mapping being intentionally left out of the capture path — the app's own Contact Profile wire shape (`{ fullName, email, phone, location, linkedin, github, website }`) has no twitter/x field at all, and no test or comment in either file mentions twitter/x, confirming the gap was never considered rather than deliberately scoped out.

## Suggested fix direction

Add a word-boundary-anchored twitter/x row to `NAMED_KEY_PATTERNS` (e.g. matching `x`/`twitter` as a standalone token, careful not to collide with unrelated short labels) so the field resolves to a recognized key and is excluded by `isCapturable` the same way linkedin/github/website already are. This key doesn't need a corresponding Contact Profile field or autofill wiring — it only needs to make the capture-exclusion path treat it as a link field instead of a genuine open-ended question.

title: desktop: draft-answer failure always says "please retry" even for a dead API key
body:
## Summary

Drafting an AI answer in the extension's Answers tab always shows the same fixed message, "Could not draft an answer. Please retry.", for every compose failure -- including a provider auth/config error (e.g. an invalid API key returning 401) that retrying can never fix. The desktop backend already classifies the underlying error as non-retriable (`AppError::Config`, for which `AppError::retriable()` returns `false`) before it reaches the compose path, but `answer_assist`'s failure handling discards that classification and always emits the same generic sentinel. The user is repeatedly told to do something guaranteed to fail, and -- because the provider's daily budget is charged before each attempt -- every retry the message invites also spends one unit of that limited quota on a call that cannot succeed.

## Environment

extension 0.154.0 store build, desktop app 0.154.0, Windows 11, Chrome

## Steps to reproduce

1. Configure the AI provider with an invalid/unauthorized API key (any call returns 401/403).
2. Open the extension side panel, go to the Answers tab on an application form, and click "Draft this answer" on any row.

## Expected

A non-retriable configuration/auth failure (bad API key, expired credentials) should be told apart from a transient generation hiccup -- e.g. pointing the user at Settings -> AI Provider -- rather than showing text that literally invites a retry guaranteed to fail identically.

## Actual

The row shows the exact same generic text every attempt: "Could not draft an answer. Please retry." The real, actionable reason (a provider-reported "invalid or unauthorized API key" message) only reaches the desktop app's log at WARN level and never reaches the extension UI. Reproduced twice, byte-identical failure and message both times, roughly 40 seconds apart.

## Root cause

- A provider 401/403 is mapped to `AppError::Config(...)` (`apps/desktop/src-tauri/src/commands/ai_provider/mod.rs:1291`), which the shared error type already classifies as not retriable (`AppError::retriable()`, `apps/desktop/src-tauri/src/error.rs:82-85`, true only for `Network`/`RateLimited`).
- That typed error survives unchanged through the compose stream (`apps/desktop/src-tauri/src/extension_bridge/stream.rs:730-745` returns the underlying `Err(e)` as-is).
- `compose_attempts` (`apps/desktop/src-tauri/src/extension_bridge/answer_assist.rs:1027-1067`) passes every non-length-cut compose failure through `to_draft_failed` (lines 1039, 1065), which (lines 170-173) logs the real cause and unconditionally replaces it with the fixed `DRAFT_FAILED_MESSAGE` (line 154) -- with no branch on error kind.
- `charge_compose_budget` (lines 905-909) charges the provider's daily ceiling before each attempt, so every doomed retry the message invites also burns quota.

## Suggested fix direction

Before collapsing in `to_draft_failed`, branch on the error's retriability (`AppError::retriable()`/kind) and return a second fixed sentinel for non-retriable compose failures (e.g. pointing at Settings -> AI) instead of the generic "please retry" text -- mirroring the existing `NO_PROVIDER_MESSAGE` vs `AI_ASSIST_OFF_MESSAGE` split (ADR-044 decision 8). This reuses classification the codebase already computes (`AppError::retriable()`/`code()`) and keeps both messages as fixed, no-dynamic-content strings, so the "nothing dynamic reaches the wire" invariant is untouched.
