title: extension: bridge reconnect never escalates backoff after a connect-then-fail handshake
body:
## Summary

After the extension's bridge client opens a transport (native messaging or the loopback WebSocket) but then fails the v2 HMAC handshake, every reconnect attempt retries at the backoff ladder's floor (500ms) forever instead of escalating up to the documented 10s cap. The exponential backoff exists in code (`BACKOFF_MS = [500, 1000, 2000, 5000, 10000]`) but never actually escalates for this failure class, because the retry counter is reset back to zero at the start of every connection attempt, before that attempt's outcome is known.

## Environment

Extension 0.154.0 (store build), desktop app 0.154.0, Windows 11, Chrome.

## Steps to reproduce

1. Pair the extension with the desktop app (a valid pairing token is stored).
2. Regenerate the pairing token in the desktop app (Settings, or a factory reset) while the extension's browser is closed or its service worker is asleep, so the live `token.revoked` frame is never delivered to it (this is the already-documented "offline at rotation" case).
3. Reopen the browser / let the service worker wake. The extension reconnects with the now-stale token: the desktop bridge accepts the transport connection, rejects the HMAC proof, and closes the socket without a reply (the deliberately silent, ambiguous close the protocol uses for a bad proof).
4. Observe the reconnect timer interval and/or the desktop app's `extension_bridge` warning logs over the next several minutes.

## Expected

Each reconnect attempt after a connect-then-fail handshake should back off further up the ladder (500ms -> 1s -> 2s -> 5s -> 10s) and settle at roughly one attempt every 10 seconds.

## Actual (with frequency)

Every reconnect after a connect-then-fail handshake retries at the ladder's floor, ~500ms, indefinitely -- it never advances to the higher rungs. This reproduces on the very first retry cycle and on every one after it (deterministic in code). It is consistent with real desktop-log bursts showing dozens of connection/handshake warning lines within a single minute, sustained for roughly an hour at a time, rather than the sparse, decreasing-frequency pattern a working backoff would produce.

## Evidence

Desktop `extension_bridge` warning log pattern during an affected window (sanitized, no tokens/paths):

```
[WARN] [extension_bridge] read error: WebSocket protocol error: Connection reset without closing handshake
[WARN] [extension_bridge] handshake: client proof failed constant-time verification
```

These repeat at intervals consistent with a fixed ~500ms retry rate rather than an escalating one, including runs of the client-proof warning only about a second apart -- the ladder's floor, never its higher rungs.

## Root cause

`apps/extension/src/lib/bridge.ts`: `attach()` (~line 2101) unconditionally resets `this.backoffIndex = 0` at line 2103, on every connection attempt, before that attempt's handshake result is known. Any handshake failure that reaches `finishHandshake('app_not_running')` (the timeout/closed/ambiguous-silence branches inside `performHandshake()`, ~lines 2200-2262) then calls `scheduleReconnect()` (~lines 2695-2703), which reads `backoffIndex` -- already reset to 0 moments earlier by that same `attach()` call -- so it always resolves to `BACKOFF_MS[0]` (500ms, line 89). `scheduleReconnect()` does increment the index afterward, but the next retry cycle calls `attach()` again, which resets it to 0 before the next `scheduleReconnect()` call runs, discarding the increment every time. (The sibling failure path in `doConnect()`, where no transport can even be opened at all, calls `scheduleReconnect()` directly without going through `attach()` and backs off correctly -- only the "transport opened, handshake then failed" class is affected.)

## Suggested fix direction

Move the `backoffIndex` reset out of `attach()`'s entry and into the handshake's actual success path only: inside `performHandshake()`'s success branch (alongside setting `authenticated = true`) and in `attach()`'s no-token early return (which also reaches `connected` without a handshake). That lets `scheduleReconnect()`'s increment persist across repeated connect-then-fail cycles so the existing `BACKOFF_MS` ladder escalates as designed. Add a test that drives two consecutive connect-then-fail handshake cycles and asserts the second reconnect waits longer than the first, since the current suite only ever exercises a single cycle.

## Related UX effect

During such a storm the popup shows "App not running" (with a Retry button) for as long as the loop lasts, although the desktop app is running. The silent close on a bad proof is deliberately ambiguous (so it cannot act as a token oracle), and the client maps it to `app_not_running`. With a working backoff this would be a short blip; with the stuck 500 ms loop it becomes the steady state. A bounded-retry hint ("re-pair?") after N consecutive connect-then-fail cycles, already a recorded follow-up under "Revocation reach" in `docs/knowledge/extension-domain.md`, would give the user a way out.

title: extension: popup/panel actions can hit another Chrome window's tab (Import writes the wrong job)
body:
## Summary
The side panel's action handlers (Check fit, and by the same code path Import/Fill/Save answers) resolve "the active tab" inside the background service worker via `browser.tabs.query({ active: true, currentWindow: true })`. A service worker has no window of its own, so Chrome's `currentWindow` falls back to whichever window last had OS focus — not necessarily the window the side panel instance is actually docked to. When a second Chrome window has focus, the panel's action buttons read (or fail to read) the wrong window's tab instead of the tab the panel is following.

## Environment
Extension 0.154.0 (store build), desktop app 0.154.0, Windows 11, Chrome.

## Steps to reproduce
1. Open the side panel in Chrome window 1 on a job posting; the panel correctly shows it is following that tab.
2. Open a different job posting in a new Chrome window (window 2), which becomes the OS-focused window. Do not interact with window 1 again.
3. Without refocusing window 1, click "Check fit" in window 1's still-open panel.

## Expected
The panel lives in window 1 and is following window 1's tab, so "Check fit" should act on window 1's tab regardless of which window currently has OS focus.

## Actual
The panel's tab caption degrades to a bare hostname instead of the tracked posting's title, a spurious empty "Form" group appears, and the action fails with "Could not read the current tab URL." Refocusing window 1 and retrying succeeds immediately with the correct result. Observed twice in a row while window 2 held focus; not reproduced once window 1 regained focus. This is a multi-window edge case, not something a single-window user will hit.

## Evidence
- Thrown error text: `Could not read the current tab URL.`
- Panel caption after the failure: `Reading: www.linkedin.com` (bare host, not the tracked posting's title)

## Root cause
`apps/extension/src/background.ts` resolves "the active tab" via `browser.tabs.query({ active: true, currentWindow: true })` in 13 separate helpers (e.g. `activeTabUrl` at background.ts:449, `captureActiveTabHtml` at background.ts:460, `activeTabIdAndUrl` at background.ts:492, used by `runMatchLive` at background.ts:1406 for Check-fit). Running in the background service worker, `currentWindow` there resolves to the last OS-focused window, not the side panel's own window. The side panel already tracks its own window id correctly for its display/follow logic (`panelWindowId`, `apps/extension/src/sidepanel/sidepanel.ts:474`, queried with `windowId: panelWindowId` at sidepanel.ts:489) but never sends that id along with action requests (`apps/extension/src/lib/messages.ts`'s `PopupRequest` carries no window id field), so the background handlers have no way to target the right window.

## Suggested fix direction
Add an optional `windowId` to the relevant `PopupRequest` messages and have the side panel pass its own `panelWindowId`. Have the affected `background.ts` helpers accept an optional `windowId` and query `{ active: true, windowId }` when supplied, keeping `currentWindow: true` as the fallback for the popup (which is always opened in the focused window by construction).

title: extension: applied.check misses a tracked LinkedIn posting on a regional host redirect
body:
## Summary

The extension's `applied.check` (and its batch form `applied.check.batch`, used for results-page stamping) looks up a tracked/applied posting by an exact normalized-URL string match. LinkedIn's own host redirects (e.g. a `de.linkedin.com` posting later opened as `www.linkedin.com`) produce two different normalized keys, so a posting that is genuinely already tracked shows up as untracked in the popup and side panel.

## Environment

Extension 0.154.0 (store build == repo main for `apps/extension` and `extension_bridge`), desktop app 0.154.0, Windows 11, Chrome.

## Steps to reproduce

1. Track/apply to a LinkedIn posting whose URL is stored under a regional host, e.g. `de.linkedin.com/jobs/view/<slug>-<id>`.
2. Open the SAME posting again later; LinkedIn's own redirect can land the tab on a different host, e.g. `www.linkedin.com/jobs/view/<slug>-<id>/`.
3. Open the extension popup, and separately the side panel, on that tab.

## Expected

The popup's page-context card and the side panel's stage strip should recognize the posting as already tracked, since it is the same job under a different LinkedIn host spelling.

## Actual

Both popup and side panel show the generic "Import the job on this page…" controls with no page-context card and no stage strip -- identical to a genuinely untracked posting. This is deterministic: it reproduces on 100% of host-spelling mismatches for LinkedIn regional/apex-host variants.

## Root cause (repo-relative path:line refs)

- `apps/desktop/src-tauri/src/extension_bridge/applied_check.rs:72-106` (`resolve_applied_check_url`) resolves `applied.check` via `canonical_job_url` -> `normalize_job_url` -> `ApplicationStore::find_by_job_url`, an exact `WHERE job_url = ?1` match (`apps/desktop/src-tauri/src/applications/mod.rs:485-495`).
- `apps/desktop/src-tauri/src/scraping/scrape_url/mod.rs:140-149` (`canonical_job_url`) returns `None` once the path already contains `/jobs/view/`, so no id-level rewrite happens for the common direct-posting case.
- `apps/desktop/src-tauri/src/applications/job_url.rs:102` (`normalize_job_url`) strips only a leading `www.` from the host, not other LinkedIn regional subdomains, so `de.linkedin.com/...` and `linkedin.com/...` (www-stripped) normalize to two different keys.
- `apps/desktop/src-tauri/src/extension_bridge/applied_check_batch.rs:16-24` reuses the same per-url resolver for `applied.check.batch`, so results-page stamping has the identical gap.
- The identity-aware fallback that already solves this class of problem -- `job_is_applied` / `scrape_url::job_identity` (`apps/desktop/src-tauri/src/extension_bridge/agent_read.rs:469-504`, `apps/desktop/src-tauri/src/scraping/scrape_url/identity.rs:43-64`), which folds any `*.linkedin.com` host and matches on the trailing numeric id -- was built for the agent/MCP `job` resource (closing a near-identical gap) but was never wired into `applied_check.rs`.

## Suggested fix direction

In `resolve_applied_check_url`, fall back to the identity-aware match (`job_identity`) already used by `job_is_applied` when the exact `find_by_job_url` lookup misses -- ideally by sharing one lookup helper across `applied_check.rs`, `applied_check_batch.rs`, and `agent_read.rs` so the three surfaces can never disagree about the same posting again.

title: settings: give the browser extension its own settings nav item and section
body:
## Summary

The browser-extension settings have grown into a full area of their own (pairing and token, connection status, four consent switches: assisted autofill, AI answer drafting, auto-track, save-answers-on-submit, plus their notices). They still live as one section inside **Settings → Accounts**, where they are hard to find and crowd the accounts page. Give the extension its own entry in the Settings sidebar and its own section.

## Proposal

- Add a top-level **Browser extension** item to the Settings sidebar (`NAV_GROUPS` / `SectionId`), rendering the existing `ExtensionBridgeSection` (moved out of `apps/desktop/src/renderer/features/settings/components/accounts/`, where it is mounted by `AccountsSettingsTab`).
- Keep the `ajh://settings/extension` deep link (the extension popup's "Find my token" button, `FocusTarget::ExtensionPairing` in `apps/desktop/src-tauri/src/deeplink/mod.rs`) landing on the new section, with the existing focus/scroll highlight (`ui-store` flag consumed by `ExtensionBridgeSection`).
- Update the settings search index (`features/settings/lib/search-index.ts`) and the help/support content that points at the old location.
- Update every piece of copy that tells the user to go to "Settings → Accounts → Browser extension". Today that wording appears in:
  - desktop refusal strings sent to the extension: `extension_bridge/{mod,status_update,document_export,agent_read,agent_call,answer_assist,answers_save}.rs`, `tray/mod.rs`, `deeplink/mod.rs`
  - the extension: `apps/extension/src/connection-status/connection-status.ts`, `apps/extension/README.md`
  - shared protocol constants: `packages/shared/src/ipc/extension-protocol-constants.ts`
  - translations (`packages/translations/src/locales/*`), `packages/prompts/src/workspace/index.ts`
  - the landing privacy page (`apps/landing/src/components/privacy/sections/{Extension,Footer}.tsx`) and the root `README.md`

## Notes

- The published extension build embeds the old wording in its own copy. Until the next Chrome/AMO release, installed extensions will still say "Accounts". The deep link is the robust path either way.
- No behaviour change to any consent switch, gate or wire verb. This is a navigation and copy move only.

## Acceptance criteria

- Settings shows a separate **Browser extension** nav item; the Accounts page no longer contains the extension section.
- `ajh://settings/extension` opens that section and highlights the pairing area.
- No remaining "Accounts → Browser extension" wording in the repo (except changelog/history).
- Existing `ExtensionBridgeSection` tests pass; sidebar/search tests cover the new item.
